title: Dental CT scan (CBCT)
what: A 3D image of your teeth and jaws. The doctor can see the roots, canals, and bone from all sides.
why: Before implants and difficult extractions, for root canal treatment, cysts, before braces, or for the sinuses.
duration: usually 5 to 10 minutes; the scan itself takes less than a minute; results often right away
tell_doctor: If you are or might be pregnant
If you have metal crowns or implants. They slightly affect the image, but they do not rule out the scan
If it is hard for you to stand or sit still

prepare.title: Prep
prepare.text: None needed. You can eat and drink.

prepare.title: Metal
prepare.text: Take off earrings, necklaces, piercings, hair clips, glasses, and removable dentures.

bring: Your dentist's referral with the area to scan
steps: A protective apron is put on you, if it does not block the image
You sit or stand in the machine, with your chin on a rest
You bite on a piece, and your head is held in place
The machine moves around your head. Do not move or swallow
The images are processed on a computer
feel: You need to keep still for less than a minute
after: You usually get the scan on a disc or USB drive. The report comes the same day or later
Take it to your dentist or oral surgeon

faq.a: The dose is higher than a panoramic X-ray, but usually lower than a regular head CT. It is ordered when treatment needs it.

faq.q: Can just part of the jaw be scanned?
faq.a: Yes, often only a small area is scanned, which lowers the dose. Your doctor chooses the area.

reminders.text: Dental CT scan soon. Take off earrings and piercings, and bring the referral with the scan area.
